title.title: A counterexample to Lipman–Zariski in characteristic zero
title.subtitle: Claim: a normal complex surface with free tangent sheaf, $\mathrm{Der}_{\mathbb{C}}(A) \cong A^2$, that is not smooth

plain: A surface whose 'directions of motion' look exactly like a smooth surface's, yet it has a sharp point

lines.note: Lipman (1965): free tangent sheaf already forces normality

beats.text: If the vector fields form a free module of the right rank, is the variety smooth?
The claim: a surface over $\mathbb{C}$ where the answer is no

steps: Build a singular point analytically, one isolated pinch
Arrange that its vector fields still form a free module
Then make it algebraic, keeping both properties

achievement.label: Lipman–Zariski conjecture (1965)
achievement.context: Before: true for hypersurfaces, lci, klt and log canonical spaces; fails in char $p$ for $xy = z^p$
achievement.note: Necessarily not log canonical, consistent with what was known

verify.ourCheck: We graded the claim, not whether it is right

voice.text: Do free vector fields force a variety to be smooth? Expected yes in characteristic zero.
Build the singular point analytically with free vector fields, then make it algebraic.
Claimed: a complex surface where it fails.

sources.quote: Der_C(A) ≅ A² free but A_m not regular; the singularity is an isolated Gorenstein surface singularity
Lipman showed in 1965 that a free tangent sheaf forces normality
In characteristic $p$ it fails already for $xy=z^p$.
It is necessarily not log canonical, which is consistent with what was known.
Built first analytically then algebraized via completed local ring; 37 pp; no Lean.
I graded what each family claims, not whether it is right.
